core_obligations: Case (1): reduce to K represented by a strictly perfect complex E^bullet on a small open set, and choose a K-flat complex F^bullet representing M (proof lines 13426-13429).
Use the strictly-perfect computation of the internal hom to represent R-Hom(K, M) by the complex with terms the direct sums of Homs between the graded pieces (proof lines 13430-13435).

Compare the pullback of that complex with the internal hom of the pulled-back complexes, using that pullback of a finite free module is finite free, to conclude the comparison map is an isomorphism in case (1) (remaining lines of the proof up to line 13480).

Verify that the flatness hypothesis of case (2) and the finite tor dimension hypothesis of case (3) supply exactly what the computation needs, so that the same argument applies with M only bounded below.
proof_roadmap: Reduce locally and choose strictly perfect and K-flat representatives.
Write the internal hom as a explicit complex of Homs.
Compare after pullback using finiteness of the representatives.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the canonical comparison map Lh^* R-Hom(K, M) -> R-Hom(Lh^*K, Lh^*M) is an isomorphism in three separate situations: K perfect; h flat with K pseudo-coherent and M bounded below; and finite tor dimension of O_X over h^{-1}O_Y with K pseudo-coherent and M bounded below. The proof of the first case reduces locally to a strictly perfect representative of K and a K-flat representative of M, computes R-Hom(K, M) as the single complex of Homs between them, and compares the pullback with the internal hom of the pullbacks using the description of pullback of finite free modules (proof lines 13426-13480). The remaining cases require the flatness and tor dimension hypotheses to make the same computation valid. H3: the local computation and the three-way case analysis are independent research-level work, not a citation chain.
